other.name: Other business
other.desc: Anything not listed. Shows the general business prompts.

gen: What the business does, who its customers are and where the income comes from. Any single customer above 25% of revenue?
New premises, acquisitions, products, services, staff or contracts the insurer has not been told about.
Claims, declines, cancellations or special terms in the last 5 years. Anything the insurer should hear from us first.
Do customers, landlords or head contractors require specific limits, indemnities or waivers of subrogation?
If the premises or a key machine were lost for three months, could the business keep trading? Alternative premises, key suppliers, key people.
mdamage: When were building, plant and stock values last checked? Rebuild cost, replacement cost and peak stock should be current.
Who insures the building and the fit-out under the lease, and does the lease require specific cover?
Earthquake-prone status or low %NBS rating, asbestos, old wiring and roof condition.
bi: Twelve months is rarely enough after a major loss. How long to rebuild, re-source or replace key plant?
Are the figures annual gross profit with the right allowance for wages and increased cost of working?
liab: Does the limit suit the largest contract and the real exposure, including any work or sales overseas?
statutory: Health and safety system, notifiable events, critical risks and contractor management. Officers have due diligence duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.
pi: Who reviews customer contracts? Any warranties of fitness or guaranteed outcomes?
dno: Directors, any disputes, any regulator contact, and any guarantees of related-party debt.
cyber: Multi-factor authentication, backups, who holds customer data and what happens if systems are down for a week.
crime: Dual authorisation on payments and bank detail changes. Invoice fraud and impersonation are the common claims.
fleet: Driver ages, licences, private use and who is covered.
cargo: Values, routes, packaging, who arranges carriage and what the carrier’s liability limits are.
machinery: Which machine would stop trading if it failed, and how long would it take to replace?

gen: Who lives at the property, and is any part rented, used for business or left empty for long periods?
Claims, declines or cancellations in the last 5 years, and any reported incidents.
Renovations, new valuables, new vehicles or drivers, a home business.
house: When was the rebuild estimate last done? Renovations, rising building costs and special features can leave the sum insured short.
Flood, slip, coastal and liquefaction exposure. Natural Hazards Commission cover sits beneath the private policy, so check what the policy covers above it.
Roof age, wiring, plumbing, weathertightness or moisture, and any work done without consent.
Interest noted on the policy, and whether a trust or company owns the property.
contents: Walk through the rooms. Under-insurance is common with electronics, clothing, tools and kitchen items.
Single-item limits for jewellery, art, bikes, instruments and cameras.
Items taken out of the house, holiday homes and student flats.
vehicle: Check the sum insured and consider agreed value for modified or special-interest vehicles.
Young or inexperienced drivers, learner or restricted licences, and excess levels.
landlord: Written tenancy, bond and Healthy Homes compliance. Loss of rent cover.
Exposure and exclusions for tenant damage, and methamphetamine contamination limits.
boat: Where the vessel is used and kept, skipper experience, race or charter use and value basis.
valuables: Current valuations, items over standard limits, and cover away from home.
caravan: Where it is stored, how often it is towed and the towing vehicle.
